author: Dr. Ananya Rao, MD
content: SOAP NOTE - Encounter Date: 2025-08-10. Subjective: 40-year-old male presents for 6-month hypertension follow-up. Reports mild occasional headaches after long work hours. Compliant with prescribed Lisinopril. Objective: BP 138/88 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98% on room air. BMI 26.8. Assessment: Essential hypertension, suboptimally controlled; Stage 1. Plan: Increase Lisinopril from 10mg daily to 20mg daily orally after breakfast. Advise low sodium DASH diet. Order basic metabolic panel (BMP) and serum creatinine check in 4 weeks. Review in Cardiology OPD with Dr. Ananya Rao in 6 weeks.

content: SOAP NOTE - Encounter Date: 2025-07-15. Subjective: 39-year-old female presents with seasonal allergic rhinitis, frequent sneezing, nasal congestion, and itchy watery eyes. Severe drug allergy to Penicillin / Amoxicillin (causes acute urticaria and anaphylaxis). Objective: Vital signs stable, afebrile. HEENT: Swollen nasal turbinates with clear watery discharge. Assessment: Moderate allergic rhinitis. Plan: Start Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50mcg, 2 sprays per nostril once daily morning. Tab Cetirizine 10mg at night as needed. Critical allergy to Penicillin reaffirmed in medical chart.
